rounds.fact: Miniclip built its whole library around free browser-based Flash games, becoming one of the biggest casual gaming destinations before Flash was phased out industry-wide.
GameSpot launched in 1996 and became known for its numerical review scores becoming a genuine influence on game sales, sometimes controversially so.
CNET launched in 1994 as one of the first tech-focused media companies built for the web, eventually growing to include Download.com and several other well-known tech properties.
Plenty of Fish was famously built and run by a single person for years, supported entirely by ads, before eventually being sold for hundreds of millions of dollars.
Kickstarter launched in 2009 and popularized the all-or-nothing crowdfunding model, where projects only get funded if they hit their goal, a rule meant to protect backers.
